content.text:
Implement GreenCycle Operations & Content Portal as an offline-first Flask + HTMX application in the current repository. Inspect the existing codebase first and extend it if compatible; if the repo is empty or incompatible, scaffold the app from scratch. Do not ask for clarification unless the repository is broken or missing critical runtime prerequisites. Make reasonable assumptions and keep moving.
Authoritative product decisions
The authoritative UI stack is Flask-rendered Jinja templates enhanced with HTMX. The stray sentence mentioning an Angular frontend conflicts with the rest of the brief and should be ignored for this implementation.
"Offline-ready" means the application must remain fully functional without any internet dependency. All JS/CSS/editor assets must be served locally. Do not use CDNs, remote fonts, remote icon sets, third-party SaaS services, external queues, or cloud storage.
Deploy as a single local application instance backed by SQLite. Optimize SQLite for local multi-user access with WAL mode, foreign keys ON, and sensible busy timeouts, but do not design for distributed deployment.
Use a clean service-layer architecture so Flask page routes, HTMX partials, REST endpoints, and GraphQL resolvers all reuse the same business logic.
Do not invent online payment integration. "Paid" means an internal offline payment record with tender type cash, check, or invoice and a required internal receipt number.
Do not invent a credit-history feature. The brief references encrypting addresses, device identifiers, and credit history; implement a generic encrypted-field abstraction and apply it to any sensitive fields that actually exist in this project, especially addresses and any future sensitive identifiers.
The primary UI date format is MM/DD/YYYY. Persist dates/times in ISO 8601 in the database/API and format/parse at the boundary.
Primary goals
CMS workflow for municipal sustainability content with draft, review, publish, scheduled publish, and withdraw states.
Operational scheduling for resources (classrooms, instructors, time slots) with conflict detection, auto/semi-auto assignment, reschedule/substitute workflows, and visible change notices.
Service catalog and order lifecycle management with offline payment capture, tax by region, reconciliation, and KPI reporting.
Search across content and operational records with full-text search, facets, trending search terms, and zero-result query reporting.
Secure file handling, local APIs (REST + GraphQL), JWT auth for APIs, quotas, and internal outbox event delivery for offline consumers.
Non-goals for the first full implementation
No external internet integrations by default.
No remote payment gateway.
No Redis, Celery, Elasticsearch, Postgres, S3, or cloud queues.
No SPA frontend.
Recommended stack
Python 3.12+
Flask app factory pattern
SQLAlchemy 2.x ORM
Alembic or Flask-Migrate for schema migrations
Jinja templates + HTMX + local Bootstrap 5 assets
WTForms or equivalent server-side form validation
Quill or TinyMCE bundled locally for rich text editing
Bleach for HTML sanitization
argon2-cffi for password hashing
Flask-WTF CSRF protection for browser forms
PyJWT or Flask-JWT-Extended for API JWTs
APScheduler (or equivalent local scheduler) for scheduled publish, archiving, purge, queue processing, and periodic jobs
SQLite FTS5 for search
Pillow, pypdf, python-docx, python-magic (or robust equivalent) for file validation/watermark handling
cryptography/Fernet for encrypted sensitive fields
pytest for automated tests

IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md

Configuration and environment
Create config settings and example env values for at least:
SECRET_KEY
SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30
LOGIN_LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD=5
LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES=15
SQLITE_PATH
STORAGE_ROOT
REPORT_OUTPUT_ROOT
MAX_UPLOAD_MB=20
DOWNLOAD_URL_TTL_SECONDS=600
ATTACHMENT_ARCHIVE_DAYS=180
ATTACHMENT_PURGE_YEARS=7
ENABLE_FILE_PURGE=true/false
API_DAILY_QUOTA=1000
JWT_SECRET_KEY
FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY
EXTERNAL_INTEGRATIONS_ENABLED=false
WATERMARK_DEFAULT_ENABLED=false
DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE=50
AGGREGATE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=600
Bind all static assets locally. No CDN references anywhere.
Permission model
Implement RBAC with roles and explicit permissions/capabilities. Users may hold multiple roles even if the UI usually presents one primary role. Suggested capabilities:
admin.manage_users
admin.manage_roles
admin.manage_settings
admin.manage_api_keys
admin.view_audit_logs
content.create
content.edit
content.submit_review
content.review
content.publish
content.schedule
content.withdraw
content.manage_taxonomy
content.manage_homepage_placement
dispatch.manage_resources
dispatch.manage_schedule
dispatch.resolve_conflicts
dispatch.view_change_notices
orders.manage
orders.record_payment
orders.reconcile
analytics.view
analytics.export
analytics.view_financials
files.upload
files.download
files.manage_retention
api.access
Mask sensitive fields in serializers/templates unless the current user has the relevant permission.
Core database design
Create normalized models and migrations for these tables/entities. Exact naming can vary, but the data model must support all behaviors below.
Identity and security
users: id, username (unique), display_name, password_hash, is_active, failed_login_attempts, lockout_until, last_login_at, last_activity_at, created_at, updated_at
roles: id, name, description
user_roles: user_id, role_id
audit_logs: id, actor_user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, details_json, created_at
settings: key, value_json, updated_by, updated_at
Regions and taxonomy
regions: id, code, name, sales_tax_rate, active
categories: id, name, slug, parent_id nullable, active
tags: id, name, slug, active
CMS content
content_items: id, slug unique, current_version_id nullable, published_version_id nullable, workflow_state, region_id nullable, media_type, is_pinned, is_recommended, is_carousel, carousel_rank nullable, created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at, published_at nullable, scheduled_publish_at nullable, withdrawn_at nullable
content_versions: id, content_item_id, version_number, title, summary, body_html, body_text, metadata_json, author_id, review_notes, workflow_state, submitted_at nullable, reviewed_by nullable, reviewed_at nullable, approved_at nullable, scheduled_publish_at nullable, published_at nullable, withdrawn_at nullable, created_at
content_categories: content_item_id, category_id
content_tags: content_item_id, tag_id
content_attachments: content_item_id, attachment_id
Search and search analytics
search_documents: id, record_type, record_id, title, body_text, tags_text, metadata_text, region_id nullable, media_type nullable, primary_date nullable, updated_at
SQLite FTS5 virtual table over title/body/tags/metadata
search_queries: id, user_id nullable, raw_query, normalized_query, filters_json, result_count, zero_results, created_at
optional precomputed search_trends table if useful, otherwise derive from search_queries
Scheduling and operations
resources: id, resource_type (classroom, instructor, other), name, code, region_id, active, metadata_json
resource_availability: id, resource_id, day_of_week, start_time, end_time, effective_from nullable, effective_to nullable
time_slot_templates: id, name, region_id nullable, start_time, end_time, active
schedule_items: id, title, region_id, scheduled_date, start_time, end_time, classroom_id nullable, instructor_id nullable, time_slot_template_id nullable, status, source_order_id nullable, notes, created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at
schedule_conflicts: id, schedule_item_id, conflict_type, related_schedule_item_id nullable, related_resource_id nullable, severity, message, resolved_at nullable, resolved_by nullable
schedule_changes: id, schedule_item_id, change_type, old_values_json, new_values_json, notice_text, changed_by, changed_at
Service catalog and orders
service_items: id, code, name, description, pricing_model (hourly, per_use, package), unit_rate nullable, package_price nullable, taxable, active, metadata_json
orders: id, order_number unique, customer_name, customer_org nullable, encrypted_service_address nullable, region_id, state, scheduled_date nullable, subtotal_amount, tax_rate, tax_amount, total_amount, paid_amount, reconciliation_status, reconciliation_delta, created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at, paid_at nullable, completed_at nullable, canceled_at nullable, refunded_at nullable, notes
order_items: id, order_id, service_item_id, description_snapshot, quantity, unit_rate, line_subtotal, taxable, metadata_json
payments: id, order_id, tender_type (cash, check, invoice), receipt_number, amount, reference_note nullable, recorded_by, recorded_at
reconciliation_runs: id, run_label, created_by, created_at, notes
reconciliation_items: id, reconciliation_run_id, order_id, expected_amount, actual_amount, delta_amount, flagged_for_review, status
Analytics/reporting
kpi_snapshots: id, report_scope, filters_hash, filters_json, metrics_json, generated_at, expires_at
report_jobs: id, report_type, filters_json, requested_by, status, row_count nullable, result_file_path nullable, error_text nullable, created_at, started_at nullable, finished_at nullable, expires_at nullable
Files
attachments: id, owner_type nullable, owner_id nullable, original_filename, stored_filename, storage_path, file_ext, mime_type, size_bytes, sha256, duplicate_of_id nullable, watermark_on_download, uploaded_by, uploaded_at, archived_at nullable, purge_after nullable, deleted_at nullable
file_download_audits: id, attachment_id, user_id, watermark_applied, downloaded_at
API and offline integrations
api_clients: id, name, key_id unique, secret_hash, scopes_json, active, last_used_at nullable, created_by, created_at
api_usage_counters: id, api_client_id, usage_date, request_count
outbox_events: id, topic, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, payload_json, status, available_at, delivered_at nullable, attempts, last_error nullable, consumer_name nullable
webhook_subscriptions (optional but recommended): id, consumer_name, endpoint_url, secret, active, local_only
Workflow rules and state machines
CMS state machine
draft -> in_review
in_review -> draft (changes requested)
in_review -> published
in_review -> scheduled
published -> withdrawn
scheduled -> published (automatic when scheduled_publish_at arrives)
scheduled -> withdrawn (if canceled before publish)
withdrawn -> draft (new revision) if the business flow needs revival
Rules:
Editors can create/edit drafts and submit for review.
Reviewers can approve, reject back to draft, schedule, publish immediately, and withdraw.
Publishing creates/updates published_version_id.
Every edit after publication creates a new version; never mutate the historical published version in place.
Slugs must be unique and validated inline.
Placements (pinned, recommended, carousel) must be manageable on published/scheduled content and reflected on homepage queries.
Order state machine
created -> paid
created -> canceled
paid -> completed
paid -> refunded
completed -> refunded (allowed if the business later requires refund after completion)
canceled is terminal
Rules:
Transition to paid requires at least one payment record with tender_type in {cash, check, invoice} and a receipt number.
Sales tax defaults from region but can be zero/null if the region does not tax the service.
Order totals are snapshot-based; changes to service catalog pricing must not retroactively alter historical orders.
Reconciliation flags any absolute delta > 5.00 for review.
Schedule lifecycle
draft -> scheduled
scheduled -> conflict (system-detected)
conflict -> scheduled (after resolution)
scheduled -> completed
scheduled/conflict -> canceled
Rules:
Conflicts include double-booked instructor, overlapping room usage, and time-slot violations.
Every reschedule/substitute action writes a schedule_changes record and exposes a visible change notice in the UI.
Auto-scheduling must never silently discard unschedulable items; leave them unassigned with explicit conflict messaging.
Authentication and session requirements
Strictly local username/password authentication only.
Hash passwords with Argon2 (preferred) or another strong salted password hash if Argon2 is unavailable.
Lock accounts for 15 minutes after 5 failed login attempts.
Enforce 30-minute idle session timeout. Update last_activity_at on each authenticated request.
Use CSRF protection for browser forms.
Set secure cookie flags appropriate for the deployment mode.
Log successful logins, failed logins, lockouts, password changes, and permission-sensitive actions to audit_logs.
Sensitive data protection
Build a reusable encrypted field helper/type and use it for service addresses and any other sensitive fields.
Only decrypt when needed and authorized.
Mask sensitive data in list views and exports unless the user has analytics.view_financials or another explicit permission.
Signed download URLs must still check current permissions at download time; signature validity alone is not sufficient.
Page map and user flows
Build server-rendered pages with HTMX-enhanced partials. Use local Bootstrap modal/dialog patterns and hx-get/hx-post/hx-swap for partial updates.

HTMX behavior requirements
Inline validation for username uniqueness, slug uniqueness, receipt number presence, tax/rate calculations, schedule constraints, and date parsing.
Modal edit forms for taxonomy, resources, payment entry, and conflict resolution.
Near-instant filter refresh for content lists, order lists, search results, schedule boards, and KPI widgets without full page reload.
Poll report jobs and scheduled publish status using lightweight HTMX polling endpoints.
Return partial templates for list/table/kanban/calendar fragments; keep full-page and partial rendering separated cleanly.
CMS implementation details
Rich text editor must run locally with no CDN assets.
Sanitize stored HTML and also derive body_text for search indexing.
Support draft save, submit for review, approve, schedule publish, immediate publish, withdraw, and version history.
Allow category/tag assignment and homepage placement flags.
Support media type classification (for search filters) and region tagging.
Build homepage query logic to surface pinned, recommended, and carousel items deterministically.
Scheduled publish should be processed by a local scheduled job at least once per minute.
Search implementation details
Use SQLite FTS5 for full-text indexing.
Maintain a unified search_documents projection table for content and operational records so the search UI can query across both.
Index titles, body text, tag text, and metadata text.
Implement facets for category, date range, region, and media type.
Log every search to search_queries with filters and result count.
Trending terms can be computed from search_queries over a rolling 7-day and 30-day window.
Zero-result queries should be queryable in an insights screen for content gap review.
Highlight matched snippets in results where practical.
Dispatch and scheduling implementation details
Resources must be reusable and typed. At minimum support classrooms and instructors. Design extensibly for more resource types.
Time slot templates define allowable windows.
Schedule UI should provide day/week views and a conflict panel.
Conflict detection must check:
same instructor assigned to overlapping schedule items
same classroom assigned to overlapping schedule items
item outside chosen time slot template or outside resource availability
Auto-scheduling phase 1 can use a deterministic greedy heuristic rather than a full optimization solver:
sort unscheduled items by priority/date rigidity
build candidate assignments from available classrooms/instructors/time slots
score candidates by least conflicts, region match, and continuity
assign best valid candidate or leave unscheduled with explicit reason
Semi-automatic scheduling should present top suggestions and let the Dispatcher confirm.
Reschedule and substitute workflows must preserve auditability via schedule_changes and update conflict status immediately.
Display clear on-screen change notices after each schedule modification.
Service catalog, pricing, orders, and reconciliation
Service items support pricing models: hourly, per_use, package.
Order line calculations:
hourly: quantity represents hours, subtotal = hours * unit_rate
per_use: quantity * unit_rate
package: fixed package_price per line unless quantity > 1 is explicitly allowed
Region sales tax rate is optional and applied at order calculation time.
Payments are internal records only; support cash, check, invoice.
Receipt number is required for payment recording and should be unique enough for auditing (enforce uniqueness if business-safe, otherwise at least validate format and flag duplicates).
Reconciliation workflow:
user creates a reconciliation run
actual amounts are entered/imported
system compares expected vs actual
absolute delta > 5.00 is flagged_for_review
Provide mismatch review screens and filtering.
KPI reporting and analytics
Implement KPI definitions clearly and document them in code/docs. Suggested baseline definitions:
turnaround_time: completed_at - created_at for orders, with average/median by filter scope
on_time_rate: percent of orders/schedule items completed on or before scheduled_date/end time
exception_rate: percent of orders/schedule items with cancellation, refund, conflict, or reconciliation issue
cost_revenue views: revenue from orders.total_amount, optional cost fields if present, otherwise implement revenue-centric reporting first and structure for future cost inputs
Requirements:
multi-dimensional filters (date range, region, service type, order state, schedule status, resource, category where relevant)
paginate tabular reports by default at 50 rows/page
server-side caching of common aggregates for 10 minutes
CSV export for authorized users
role-based hiding of sensitive financial fields
asynchronous report generation for queries expected to exceed 5 seconds
Implementation suggestion:
implement a report estimator based on row count or complexity
if estimated cost is low, generate synchronously
otherwise create a report_jobs row, return queued status, and let HTMX poll job status until a downloadable CSV is ready
Report job processing
Build a lightweight SQLite-backed job queue in report_jobs.
Background worker thread/process reads queued jobs, marks running/completed/failed, writes CSV to storage/generated_reports, and exposes a signed download action.
Include expiry/cleanup for old generated reports.
Surface job status and errors clearly in the UI.
File governance and downloads
Enforce all of the following:
Whitelist: PDF, JPG/JPEG, PNG, DOCX only
Max size 20 MB
Explicit blocklist for executables and suspicious archive/script types
Validate MIME type and extension consistency
Compute SHA-256 fingerprint for every upload
Detect duplicates by sha256 and surface duplicate_of_id or a warning
Store files under a non-public local directory
Archive after 180 days
Purge after 7 years only if configured
Signed, time-limited download URLs valid for 10 minutes
Permission checks on every download
Optional visible watermark applied on download rather than mutating the stored original
Watermark implementation guidance:
PDF: generate a temporary stamped copy on demand
JPG/PNG: generate a temporary watermarked image on demand
DOCX: if practical, generate a temporary stamped copy using python-docx; if implementation becomes unstable, document a narrow fallback and keep the service abstraction ready
Also:
Never serve user uploads directly from the web server static path.
Record download audits.
Use safe filenames and path traversal protection.
REST API requirements
Create local-only JSON APIs under /api/v1. These should back integration use cases and reuse the same service layer as the HTML UI.
Suggested endpoints:
POST /api/v1/auth/token for API client credentials to JWT exchange
GET /api/v1/content
GET /api/v1/content/<id>
POST /api/v1/content
POST /api/v1/content/<id>/submit-review
POST /api/v1/content/<id>/approve
POST /api/v1/content/<id>/schedule
POST /api/v1/content/<id>/withdraw
GET /api/v1/search
GET /api/v1/search/insights
GET /api/v1/resources
POST /api/v1/resources
GET /api/v1/schedules
POST /api/v1/schedules/auto-assign
POST /api/v1/schedules/<id>/reschedule
POST /api/v1/schedules/<id>/substitute
GET /api/v1/service-items
GET /api/v1/orders
POST /api/v1/orders
POST /api/v1/orders/<id>/pay
POST /api/v1/orders/<id>/cancel
POST /api/v1/orders/<id>/complete
POST /api/v1/orders/<id>/refund
POST /api/v1/reconciliation-runs
GET /api/v1/kpis
POST /api/v1/reports
GET /api/v1/reports/<id>
GET /api/v1/files/<id>/download-link
GET /api/v1/outbox-events/pull
POST /api/v1/outbox-events/<id>/ack
Protect every API route with JWT + scope/permission checks + quota enforcement.
GraphQL requirements
Implement a minimal GraphQL endpoint alongside REST using the same service layer. Keep schema practical rather than huge. At minimum support:
Queries
content(id, slug)
contents(filters)
search(query, filters)
schedules(filters)
orders(filters)
reportJob(id)
Mutations
createReportJob
acknowledgeOutboxEvent
optional content workflow and schedule update mutations if easy once services exist
GraphQL should be local-only, JWT-protected, and quota-limited just like REST.
API auth and quotas
Admin creates api_clients with key_id and secret.
Client exchanges credentials for JWT.
JWT includes scopes and expiry.
Every authenticated API request increments usage in api_usage_counters.
Enforce 1,000 requests/day per API key.
Return clear 429 responses when quota is exceeded.
Log API access and failures to audit logs where appropriate.
Offline webhook-style integrations via outbox
Implement webhook-style event delivery as an internal outbox/queue for offline consumers.
When notable events occur (content published, schedule changed, order paid/completed/refunded, report completed), write an outbox_events row.
Primary offline consumption mode: consumers poll /api/v1/outbox-events/pull and ack processed events.
Optional local push mode: if webhook_subscriptions are configured and EXTERNAL_INTEGRATIONS_ENABLED is true, attempt delivery only to local/internal endpoints, never internet hosts by default.
Retry failed deliveries with capped attempts and status tracking.
Caching strategy
Use Flask-Caching filesystem cache or an equivalent local server-side cache for aggregates.
Cache common KPI aggregate results for 10 minutes using a stable key from report type + filters + permission scope.
Do not cache per-user sensitive datasets in a way that can leak across roles.
Invalidate or bypass cache when underlying data changes materially or when permissions differ.
Background jobs and scheduling
Use a local scheduler and keep the app operational without external workers. Required jobs:
scheduled content publish/withdraw processor (every minute)
report job processor (frequent polling)
attachment archive processor (daily)
attachment purge processor (daily, only if enabled)
optional cache warmer for common KPI views
Ensure jobs are idempotent and recorded in logs. Because SQLite is the datastore, avoid complex concurrent writers.
Validation and UI details
All date inputs shown as MM/DD/YYYY, parsed carefully, and validated server-side.
Tables paginate at 50 rows/page by default.
Filters persist in query strings where possible.
Use empty-state messaging, especially for zero-result searches, no conflicts, and no pending review items.
Prefer accessible form labels, keyboard-usable modals, and visible error summaries.
Keep templates modular with reusable macros/components for badges, tables, pagination, and permission-gated actions.
Performance and robustness
Enable SQLite WAL mode and foreign keys.
Add indexes for common filters: workflow state, region, schedule date, order state, payment receipt, created_at, published_at.
Keep FTS projections in sync via service-layer upserts or DB triggers.
Avoid N+1 query patterns in list views.
Keep uploads and generated reports outside the code directory.
Sanitize any HTML output from the CMS before rendering.
Testing requirements
Add meaningful automated coverage. At minimum:
Unit tests
password hash/verify
login lockout after 5 failures
idle session timeout
RBAC permission checks
content workflow transitions
order workflow transitions
tax calculation and reconciliation flag threshold
conflict detection rules
signed download URL expiry and permission re-check
quota enforcement
encrypted field round-trip
Integration tests
login/logout flow
HTMX partial responses for inline validation and filtered lists
CMS create -> review -> publish flow
scheduled publish job
schedule conflict resolution flow
order payment and reconciliation flow
report async generation and CSV download
file upload validation and duplicate detection
REST JWT auth and GraphQL auth
Use seed fixtures for representative users, content, resources, schedules, orders, and attachments.
Seed/demo data
Provide a seed command that creates:
one admin, one editor, one reviewer, one dispatcher, one analyst
sample regions with different tax rates
sample categories and tags
several content items in draft/review/published/scheduled states
classrooms, instructors, time slots, and a few conflicting schedule items
service items for hourly/per_use/package pricing
orders in created/paid/completed/refunded states
sample report jobs and search queries for dashboard/demo purposes
Documentation to produce while implementing
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: modules, services, jobs, security decisions
docs/API.md: REST + GraphQL auth, endpoints, scopes, quota behavior
docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md: checklist of phases completed and pending
setup instructions for local run, migrations, seeding, and scheduler behavior
Implementation sequence
Work in phases and keep the app runnable after each phase. Do not try to finish everything in one monolithic patch.
Phase 0 - repository assessment and scaffolding
Inspect current repo and preserve compatible code.
Create/update project structure, config, extension wiring, local assets, and base layout.
Create docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md with a checklist mirroring these phases.
Add basic app factory, environment config, DB init, migration tooling, and test harness.
Phase 1 - identity, RBAC, admin foundation
Implement users, roles, permissions, login/logout, lockout, idle timeout, audit logging.
Build admin screens for users/roles/settings/regions.
Add seeded accounts and smoke tests.
Phase 2 - CMS core
Implement categories/tags/regions/media types, content models/versioning, rich text editor integration, content CRUD, draft/review/publish/schedule/withdraw flow, homepage placement, and review queue.
Add HTMX inline validation and modal taxonomy editing.
Add scheduled publish processor.
Phase 3 - search and search insights
Implement search_documents projection + FTS5.
Index CMS content first, then add operational records.
Build /search UI, facets, logging, trending terms, and zero-result insights.
Phase 4 - resources and scheduling
Implement resources, availability, time slot templates, schedule items, conflict detection, schedule board, conflict panel, auto/semi-auto scheduling, reschedule/substitute workflows, and change notices.
Phase 5 - service catalog, orders, payments, reconciliation
Implement service items, order creation/editing, pricing logic, tax by region, offline payment capture, order state machine, reconciliation runs, and mismatch review.
Phase 6 - analytics and reports
Implement KPI services, dashboards, multi-dimensional filters, caching, CSV exports, report_jobs queue, async generation, and download flow.
Apply masking of sensitive financial fields by role.
Phase 7 - files and retention
Implement attachment upload validation, hashing, duplicate detection, storage service, signed download URLs, watermarking, archive/purge jobs, and download audits.
Phase 8 - local REST/GraphQL APIs and outbox
Implement JWT auth for API clients, scope checks, quota counters, REST endpoints, GraphQL endpoint, outbox event creation, poll/ack consumption, and optional local push delivery behind feature flag.
Phase 9 - hardening and polish
Finish audit coverage, pagination consistency, index tuning, empty states, seed data quality, and docs.
Expand tests across all major workflows.
Acceptance criteria
The implementation is done when all of the following are true:
A local user can log in, remain active, time out after inactivity, and get locked out after repeated failed logins.
Editors can create rich-text content, submit it for review, reviewers can publish/schedule/withdraw it, and published content appears in homepage queries with placement flags.
Search returns content and operational results, supports all required facets, logs queries, shows trending terms, and surfaces zero-result searches.
Dispatchers can manage resources and schedules, run auto/semi-auto assignment, see conflicts, and resolve them through reschedule/substitute flows with visible change notices.
Service items and orders support hourly/per_use/package pricing, tax by region, offline payment recording, lifecycle transitions, and reconciliation mismatch review for deltas greater than 5.00.
Analysts can view KPI dashboards, filter results, export CSVs, and receive async downloadable report results for expensive queries.
Attachments enforce whitelist/size/MIME rules, duplicate detection, signed time-limited downloads, permission checks, optional watermarking, and retention jobs.

from datetime import datetime
from flask_login import UserMixin
from app.extensions import db

user_roles = db.Table(
    "user_roles",
    db.Column("user_id", db.Integer, db.ForeignKey("users.id"), primary_key=True),
    db.Column("role_id", db.Integer, db.ForeignKey("roles.id"), primary_key=True),
)


# Capability constants
CAPABILITIES = [
    "admin.manage_users",
    "admin.manage_roles",
    "admin.manage_settings",
    "admin.manage_api_keys",
    "admin.view_audit_logs",
    "content.create",
    "content.edit",
    "content.submit_review",
    "content.review",
    "content.publish",
    "content.schedule",
    "content.withdraw",
    "content.manage_taxonomy",
    "content.manage_homepage_placement",
    "dispatch.manage_resources",
    "dispatch.manage_schedule",
    "dispatch.resolve_conflicts",
    "dispatch.view_change_notices",
    "orders.manage",
    "orders.record_payment",
    "orders.reconcile",
    "analytics.view",
    "analytics.export",
    "analytics.view_financials",
    "files.upload",
    "files.download",
    "files.manage_retention",
    "api.access",
]

role_permissions = db.Table(
    "role_permissions",
    db.Column("role_id", db.Integer, db.ForeignKey("roles.id"), primary_key=True),
    db.Column("permission", db.String(100), primary_key=True),
)


class Role(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = "roles"
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(50), unique=True, nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.String(255))
    permissions = db.relationship(
        "RolePermission", backref="role", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )
    users = db.relationship("User", secondary=user_roles, back_populates="roles")

    def get_permissions(self):
        return {rp.permission for rp in self.permissions}


class RolePermission(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = "role_permissions_detail"
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    role_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey("roles.id"), nullable=False)
    permission = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=False)

    __table_args__ = (db.UniqueConstraint("role_id", "permission"),)


class User(UserMixin, db.Model):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False, index=True)
    display_name = db.Column(db.String(120), nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    is_active_user = db.Column(db.Boolean, default=True, nullable=False)
    failed_login_attempts = db.Column(db.Integer, default=0, nullable=False)
    lockout_until = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=True)
    last_login_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=True)
    last_activity_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=True)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(
        db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow, nullable=False
    )
    roles = db.relationship("Role", secondary=user_roles, back_populates="users")

    @property
    def is_active(self):
        return self.is_active_user

    def get_permissions(self):
        perms = set()
        for role in self.roles:
            perms.update(role.get_permissions())
        return perms

    def has_permission(self, perm: str) -> bool:
        return perm in self.get_permissions()

    def has_any_permission(self, *perms: str) -> bool:
        user_perms = self.get_permissions()
        return bool(user_perms & set(perms))


class AuditLog(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = "audit_logs"
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    actor_user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=True)
    action = db.Column(db.String(100), nullable=False, index=True)
    entity_type = db.Column(db.String(80), nullable=True)
    entity_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=True)
    details_json = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, nullable=False, index=True)

    actor = db.relationship("User", foreign_keys=[actor_user_id])


class Setting(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = "settings"
    key = db.Column(db.String(100), primary_key=True)
    value_json = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    updated_by = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=True)
    updated_at = db.Column(
        db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow
    )
"}

import os

def create_app(config_class=None):
    app = Flask(__name__, instance_relative_config=True)
    
    if config_class is None:
        config_class = TestConfig if os.environ.get("TESTING") else Config
    app.config.from_object(config_class)
    
    os.makedirs(app.instance_path, exist_ok=True)

    # Initialize extensions
    from app.extensions import db, migrate, csrf, cache, login_manager
    db.init_app(app)
    migrate.init_app(app, db)
    csrf.init_app(app)
    cache.init_app(app)
    login_manager.init_app(app)
    
    # Configure SQLite

from flask import current_app

from app.models.user import User

def authenticate_user(username, password):
    """Attempt login. Returns (user, error_message) tuple."""
    user = User.query.filter_by(username=username).first()
    if not user:
        return None, "Invalid username or password."
    
    if not user.is_active_user:
        return None, "Account is disabled."
    
    # Check lockout
    if user.lockout_until and user.lockout_until > datetime.utcnow():
        remaining = (user.lockout_until - datetime.utcnow()).seconds // 60 + 1
        log_action(user.id, "login_attempt_locked", "user", user.id)
        return None, f"Account locked. Try again in {remaining} minutes."
    
    if not verify_password(user.password_hash, password):
        user.failed_login_attempts += 1
        threshold = current_app.config["LOGIN_LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD"]
        if user.failed_login_attempts >= threshold:
            lockout_min = current_app.config["LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES"]
            user.lockout_until = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=lockout_min)
            log_action(user.id, "account_locked", "user", user.id,

        log_action(user.id, "login_failed", "user", user.id)
        return None, "Invalid username or password."
    
    # Success

    user.lockout_until = None
    user.last_login_at = datetime.utcnow()
    user.last_activity_at = datetime.utcnow()
    db.session.commit()
    log_action(user.id, "login_success", "user", user.id)
    return user, None

    """Create FTS5 virtual table if not exists. Call during app init or migration."""

            "title, body_text, tags_text, metadata_text, "
            "content='search_documents', content_rowid='id')"
        ))
        db.session.commit()


def rebuild_fts_index():

    db.session.commit()


def index_content_item(item):
    """Index or update a content item in search_documents + FTS."""
    version = item.current_version
    if not version:
        return
    tags_text = " ".join(t.name for t in item.tags) if item.tags else ""
    cat_text = " ".join(c.name for c in item.categories) if item.categories else ""
    metadata_text = f"{cat_text} {item.media_type or ''}"

    doc = SearchDocument.query.filter_by(record_type="content", record_id=item.id).first()
    if doc:

        doc.body_text = version.body_text or ""
        doc.tags_text = tags_text
        doc.metadata_text = metadata_text
        doc.region_id = item.region_id
        doc.media_type = item.media_type
        doc.primary_date = (item.published_at or item.created_at).date() if item.published_at or item.created_at else None
        doc.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()
    else:

## 2. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

```markdown
# Architecture

## Overview
GreenCycle Operations & Content Portal is an offline-first Flask application for municipal sustainability content management, operational scheduling, service catalog/order lifecycle, and analytics.

## Stack
- **Backend**: Python 3.12+, Flask 3.x, SQLAlchemy 2.x
- **Database**: SQLite with WAL mode, FTS5 for search
- **Frontend**: Jinja2 templates + HTMX + Bootstrap 5 (all served locally)
- **Rich Text**: Quill 1.3.7 (bundled)
- **Auth**: Argon2 password hashing, Flask-Login sessions, PyJWT for APIs
- **Background Jobs**: APScheduler (in-process)
- **Encryption**: cryptography/Fernet for sensitive fields

## Architecture Decisions

### Offline-First
All assets served locally. No CDNs, external APIs, SaaS services, or cloud dependencies. The application is fully functional without internet access.

### Service Layer Architecture
Flask page routes, HTMX partials, REST endpoints, and GraphQL resolvers all call the same service functions (app/services/). No business logic lives in routes.

### SQLite Optimization
- WAL mode for concurrent readers
- Foreign keys enforced
- 5-second busy timeout
- FTS5 for full-text search
- Indexes on workflow_state, dates, and foreign keys

### Authentication
- Username/password only (no OAuth/SSO)
- Argon2 for password hashing (salted, memory-hard)
- Account lockout: 5 failures -> 15 minute lockout
- Session timeout: 30 minute idle
- CSRF protection via Flask-WTF on all browser forms
- JWT for API clients (separate from session auth)

### Encrypted Fields
Fernet symmetric encryption for service addresses and other sensitive data. Encryption key from config. Only decrypted when authorized user explicitly requests it.

### Payment Model
Internal offline payment records only. Tender types: cash, check, invoice. Receipt number required. No external payment gateway integration.

### Reconciliation
Delta threshold of $5.00. Absolute difference exceeding threshold is flagged for review. Status tracked per reconciliation run.

### File Storage
Files stored in non-public directory (storage/uploads/). Never served from static path. Signed URLs with HMAC verification and expiry. Watermarks applied on-demand, never mutating originals.

### Date Handling
- UI display: MM/DD/YYYY
- Database/API: ISO 8601
- Conversion at boundary (parse_date_us / format_date_us)

## Module Map

```
app/
├── __init__.py          # App factory
├── config.py            # Configuration
├── extensions.py        # Flask extension instances
├── models/              # SQLAlchemy models
├── services/            # Business logic (reused across UI/API/GraphQL)
│   ├── auth_service.py
│   ├── admin_service.py
│   ├── cms_service.py
│   ├── search_service.py
│   ├── dispatch_service.py
│   ├── order_service.py
│   ├── analytics_service.py
│   ├── file_service.py
│   ├── outbox_service.py
│   ├── api_auth_service.py
│   └── audit_service.py
├── blueprints/          # Flask blueprints (routes only)
├── graphql/             # GraphQL schema
├── forms/               # WTForms
├── templates/           # Jinja2 templates
├── static/              # CSS, JS, vendor assets
├── tasks/               # Scheduler, seed command
└── utils/               # Helpers (encryption, dates, auth, pagination)
```

## Background Jobs
- **Scheduled Publish**: Every 1 minute, publishes content where scheduled_publish_at <= now
- **Report Processor**: Every 30 seconds, processes queued report jobs
- **Attachment Archive**: Daily at 2:00 AM, archives files older than 180 days
- **Attachment Purge**: Daily at 3:00 AM, purges files older than 7 years (if enabled)

## Security Notes
- All user inputs sanitized (Bleach for HTML, WTForms for forms)
- SQL injection prevented by SQLAlchemy ORM
- Path traversal prevented in file operations
- CSRF on all browser forms
- Signed download URLs re-check permissions
- Sensitive fields masked in list views unless authorized
- Audit logging for security-relevant actions
```

# API Documentation

## Authentication
API clients use key-based JWT authentication.

### Obtain Token
```
POST /api/v1/auth/token
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "key_id": "your_key_id",
  "secret": "your_secret"
}

Response:
{
  "token": "eyJ...",
  "expires_in": 3600
}

### Using the Token
Include in Authorization header:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
```

## Scopes
API clients are assigned scopes that control access:
- `content.read` / `content.write`
- `search.read`
- `dispatch.read` / `dispatch.write`
- `orders.read` / `orders.write`
- `analytics.read`
- `files.read`
- `outbox.read` / `outbox.write`

## Quotas
- Default: 1,000 requests/day per API key
- 429 response when quota exceeded
- Counter resets daily

## REST Endpoints

## GraphQL

### Endpoint
```
POST /api/v1/graphql
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "query": "{ contents(state: \"published\") { id title slug } }"
}
```

### Queries
- `content(id, slug)` - Single content item
- `contents(state, region_id)` - Content list
- `search(query, record_type)` - Search
- `schedules(status, region_id)` - Schedule items
- `orders(state, region_id)` - Orders
- `reportJob(id)` - Report job status

### Mutations
- `createReportJob(report_type, filters)` - Create report
- `acknowledgeOutboxEvent(id)` - Ack event

```bash

flask db upgrade  # or flask db init + migrate
flask seed
python run.py
```

## 2. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

```markdown
# Architecture

## Overview
GreenCycle Operations & Content Portal is an offline-first Flask application for municipal sustainability content management, operational scheduling, service catalog/order lifecycle, and analytics.

## Stack
- **Backend**: Python 3.12+, Flask 3.x, SQLAlchemy 2.x
- **Database**: SQLite with WAL mode, FTS5 for search
- **Frontend**: Jinja2 templates + HTMX + Bootstrap 5 (all served locally)
- **Rich Text**: Quill 1.3.7 (bundled)
- **Auth**: Argon2 password hashing, Flask-Login sessions, PyJWT for APIs
- **Background Jobs**: APScheduler (in-process)
- **Encryption**: cryptography/Fernet for sensitive fields

## Architecture Decisions

### Offline-First
All assets served locally. No CDNs, external APIs, SaaS services, or cloud dependencies. The application is fully functional without internet access.

### Service Layer Architecture
Flask page routes, HTMX partials, REST endpoints, and GraphQL resolvers all call the same service functions (app/services/). No business logic lives in routes.

### SQLite Optimization
- WAL mode for concurrent readers
- Foreign keys enforced
- 5-second busy timeout
- FTS5 for full-text search
- Indexes on workflow_state, dates, and foreign keys

### Authentication
- Username/password only (no OAuth/SSO)
- Argon2 for password hashing (salted, memory-hard)
- Account lockout: 5 failures -> 15 minute lockout
- Session timeout: 30 minute idle
- CSRF protection via Flask-WTF on all browser forms
- JWT for API clients (separate from session auth)

### Encrypted Fields
Fernet symmetric encryption for service addresses and other sensitive data. Encryption key from config. Only decrypted when authorized user explicitly requests it.

### Payment Model
Internal offline payment records only. Tender types: cash, check, invoice. Receipt number required. No external payment gateway integration.

### Reconciliation
Delta threshold of $5.00. Absolute difference exceeding threshold is flagged for review. Status tracked per reconciliation run.

### File Storage
Files stored in non-public directory (storage/uploads/). Never served from static path. Signed URLs with HMAC verification and expiry. Watermarks applied on-demand, never mutating originals.

### Date Handling
- UI display: MM/DD/YYYY
- Database/API: ISO 8601
- Conversion at boundary (parse_date_us / format_date_us)

## Module Map

```
app/
├── __init__.py          # App factory
├── config.py            # Configuration
├── extensions.py        # Flask extension instances
├── models/              # SQLAlchemy models
├── services/            # Business logic (reused across UI/API/GraphQL)
│   ├── auth_service.py
│   ├── admin_service.py
│   ├── cms_service.py
│   ├── search_service.py
│   ├── dispatch_service.py
│   ├── order_service.py
│   ├── analytics_service.py
│   ├── file_service.py
│   ├── outbox_service.py
│   ├── api_auth_service.py
│   └── audit_service.py
├── blueprints/          # Flask blueprints (routes only)
├── graphql/             # GraphQL schema
├── forms/               # WTForms
├── templates/           # Jinja2 templates
├── static/              # CSS, JS, vendor assets
├── tasks/               # Scheduler, seed command
└── utils/               # Helpers (encryption, dates, auth, pagination)
```

## Background Jobs
- **Scheduled Publish**: Every 1 minute, publishes content where scheduled_publish_at <= now
- **Report Processor**: Every 30 seconds, processes queued report jobs
- **Attachment Archive**: Daily at 2:00 AM, archives files older than 180 days
- **Attachment Purge**: Daily at 3:00 AM, purges files older than 7 years (if enabled)

## Security Notes
- All user inputs sanitized (Bleach for HTML, WTForms for forms)
- SQL injection prevented by SQLAlchemy ORM
- Path traversal prevented in file operations
- CSRF on all browser forms
- Signed download URLs re-check permissions
- Sensitive fields masked in list views unless authorized
- Audit logging for security-relevant actions
```

# API Documentation

## Authentication
API clients use key-based JWT authentication.

### Obtain Token
```
POST /api/v1/auth/token
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "key_id": "your_key_id",
  "secret": "your_secret"
}

Response:
{
  "token": "eyJ...",
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```

### Using the Token
Include in Authorization header:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
```

## Scopes
API clients are assigned scopes that control access:
- `content.read` / `content.write`
- `search.read`
- `dispatch.read` / `dispatch.write`
- `orders.read` / `orders.write`
- `analytics.read`
- `files.read`
- `outbox.read` / `outbox.write`

## Quotas
- Default: 1,000 requests/day per API key
- 429 response when quota exceeded
- Counter resets daily

8	def create_app(config_class=None):
9	    app = Flask(__name__, instance_relative_config=True)
10	
11	    if config_class is None:
12	        config_class = TestConfig if os.environ.get("TESTING") else Config
13	    app.config.from_object(config_class)
14	
15	    os.makedirs(app.instance_path, exist_ok=True)
16	    os.makedirs(str(app.config["STORAGE_ROOT"] / "uploads"), exist_ok=True)
17	    os.makedirs(str(app.config["STORAGE_ROOT"] / "archive"), exist_ok=True)
18	    os.makedirs(str(app.config["REPORT_OUTPUT_ROOT"]), exist_ok=True)
19	
20	    # Initialize extensions
21	    from app.extensions import db, migrate, csrf, cache, login_manager
22	    db.init_app(app)
23	    migrate.init_app(app, db)
24	    csrf.init_app(app)
25	    cache.init_app(app)
26	    login_manager.init_app(app)
27	
28	    # Configure SQLite
29	    with app.app_context():
30	        if "sqlite" in app.config["SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI"]:
31	            from sqlalchemy import event
32	
33	            @event.listens_for(db.engine, "connect")
34	            def set_sqlite_pragma(dbapi_connection, connection_record):
35	                cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
36	                cursor.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
37	                cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
38	                cursor.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000")
39	                cursor.close()
40	
41	    # User loader
42	    @login_manager.user_loader

Used by gunicorn: gunicorn "run:app"
Used locally:     python run.py
"""

import os
from app import create_app
from app.tasks.scheduler import init_scheduler

app = create_app()

# Initialize FTS tables
with app.app_context():
    from app.services.search_service import init_fts
    init_fts(app)

# Start background scheduler only in the main process.
# Gunicorn preload: scheduler runs in the master before fork.
# With --preload this runs once; without it each worker runs it,
# so we guard with an env flag that the entrypoint sets.
_scheduler_started = False
if not _scheduler_started:
    init_scheduler(app)
    _scheduler_started = True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True, port=5000, use_reloader=False)
"}

```python
@app.before_request
def check_session_timeout():
    from flask import session, redirect, url_for, request as req
    from flask_login import current_user, logout_user
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta

    if current_user.is_authenticated:
        now = datetime.utcnow()
        last = current_user.last_activity_at
        timeout = app.config["SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES"]
        if last and (now - last) > timedelta(minutes=timeout):
            logout_user()
            session.clear()
            if not req.path.startswith("/api/"):
                from flask import flash
                flash("Session timed out due to inactivity.", "warning")
                return redirect(url_for("auth.login"))
        current_user.last_activity_at = now
        db.session.commit()
```

**Session Configuration (File: `/c/Users/amana/OneDrive/Desktop/Files/Eaglepoint/April 3/Task-37/repo/app/config.py`, Lines 46-48):**

### 2. API JWT AUTH - Detailed Analysis

**File:** `/c/Users/amana/OneDrive/Desktop/Files/Eaglepoint/April 3/Task-37/repo/app/blueprints/api/routes.py`

**JWT Required Decorator (Lines 16-34):**
```python
def jwt_required(f):
    @wraps(f)
    def decorated(*args, **kwargs):
        auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        if not auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
            return jsonify({"error": "Missing or invalid Authorization header"}), 401
        token = auth_header[7:]
        payload, error = api_auth_service.decode_jwt(token)
        if error:
            return jsonify({"error": error}), 401

        ok, count = api_auth_service.check_quota(payload["client_id"])
        if not ok:
            return jsonify({"error": "Daily quota exceeded", "usage": count}), 429

        g.api_client_id = payload["client_id"]
        g.api_scopes = payload.get("scopes", [])
        return f(*args, **kwargs)
    return decorated
```

**Key Points:**
- `g.api_client_id` is set from JWT payload's `client_id` (line 31)
- `g.api_scopes` is set from JWT payload's `scopes` list (line 32)
- Quota check occurs on every request (line 27)
- API returns 401 on invalid/missing auth, 429 on quota exceeded

**Scope Required Decorator (Lines 37-45):**

def scope_required(scope):
    def decorator(f):
        @wraps(f)
        def decorated(*args, **kwargs):
            if scope not in g.get("api_scopes", []):
                return jsonify({"error": f"Scope '{scope}' required"}), 403
            return f(*args, **kwargs)
        return decorated
    return decorator
```

def generate_jwt(client):

    payload = {
        "sub": client.key_id,
        "client_id": client.id,
        "scopes": scopes,
        "iat": datetime.utcnow(),
        "exp": datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(
            seconds=current_app.config.get("JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_SECONDS", 3600)
        ),
    }
    token = jwt.encode(payload, current_app.config["JWT_SECRET_KEY"], algorithm="HS256")
    return token
```

        payload = jwt.decode(token, current_app.config["JWT_SECRET_KEY"], algorithms=["HS256"])
        return payload, None
    except jwt.ExpiredSignatureError:
        return None, "Token expired."
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError:

**Quota Enforcement (File: `/c/Users/amana/OneDrive/Desktop/Files/Eaglepoint/April 3/Task-37/repo/app/services/api_auth_service.py`, Lines 49-64):**

def check_quota(client_id):
    today = date.today()
    counter = ApiUsageCounter.query.filter_by(
        api_client_id=client_id, usage_date=today
    ).first()
    if not counter:
        counter = ApiUsageCounter(api_client_id=client_id, usage_date=today, request_count=0)
        db.session.add(counter)
        db.session.flush()

    quota = current_app.config.get("API_DAILY_QUOTA", 1000)
    if counter.request_count >= quota:
        return False, counter.request_count
    counter.request_count += 1
    db.session.commit()
    return True, counter.request_count
```

def validate_upload(file_storage):
    """Validate file extension, MIME, and size. Returns (ok, error_message)."""
    filename = file_storage.filename or ""
    ext = filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in filename else ""

    if ext in BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS:
        return False, f"File type .{ext} is blocked."
    if ext not in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS:
        return False, f"Only {', '.join(ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS)} files are allowed."

    content_type = file_storage.content_type or ""
    expected_mime = MIME_MAP.get(ext, "")
    if expected_mime and content_type and not content_type.startswith(expected_mime.split("/")[0]):
        return False, f"MIME type {content_type} does not match extension .{ext}."

    file_storage.seek(0, 2)
    size = file_storage.tell()
    file_storage.seek(0)
    max_bytes = current_app.config["MAX_UPLOAD_MB"] * 1024 * 1024
    if size > max_bytes:
        return False, f"File exceeds {current_app.config['MAX_UPLOAD_MB']} MB limit."

## Task 1: Create app/utils/auth_context.py - principal resolution helper

Create this new file:
```python
"""Unified principal resolution for browser sessions and API JWT contexts."""

from flask import g
from flask_login import current_user


def get_current_actor_id():
    """Return the acting user ID from either browser session or API JWT context.
    
    For browser routes: returns current_user.id from Flask-Login session.
    For API routes: returns the api_client_id stored in g by jwt_required decorator.
    
    Raises RuntimeError if no authenticated principal is available.
    """
    # Browser session
    if current_user and hasattr(current_user, 'id') and current_user.is_authenticated:
        return current_user.id
    # API JWT context (api_client_id is the ApiClient.id, which maps to created_by user)
    api_client_id = g.get("api_client_id")
    if api_client_id:
        return _resolve_api_actor(api_client_id)
    raise RuntimeError("No authenticated principal available")


def _resolve_api_actor(api_client_id):
    """Resolve the user identity behind an API client."""
    from app.models.api import ApiClient
    from app.extensions import db
    client = db.session.get(ApiClient, api_client_id)
    if client and client.created_by:
        return client.created_by
    # Fallback: return the client ID itself as actor (still traceable)
    return api_client_id


def get_api_scopes():
    """Return the scopes from the current API JWT context, or empty set."""
    return set(g.get("api_scopes", []))


def has_api_scope(scope):
    """Check if the current API context has a given scope."""
    return scope in get_api_scopes()


def is_safe_redirect_url(target):
    """Validate that a redirect target is a safe internal relative URL."""
    if not target:
        return False
    # Block absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, and javascript: schemes
    if target.startswith(("http://", "https://", "//", "javascript:")):
        return False
    # Must start with /
    if not target.startswith("/"):
        return False
    # Block backslash tricks
    if "\\" in target:
        return False
    return True
```

"""Unified principal resolution for browser sessions and API JWT contexts."""

from flask import g
from flask_login import current_user


def get_current_actor_id():
    """Return the acting user ID from either browser session or API JWT context.
    
    For browser routes: returns current_user.id from Flask-Login session.
    For API routes: returns the api_client_id stored in g by jwt_required decorator.
    
    Raises RuntimeError if no authenticated principal is available.
    """
    # Browser session
    if current_user and hasattr(current_user, 'id') and current_user.is_authenticated:
        return current_user.id
    # API JWT context (api_client_id is the ApiClient.id, which maps to created_by user)
    api_client_id = g.get("api_client_id")
    if api_client_id:
        return _resolve_api_actor(api_client_id)
    raise RuntimeError("No authenticated principal available")


def _resolve_api_actor(api_client_id):
    """Resolve the user identity behind an API client."""
    from app.models.api import ApiClient
    from app.extensions import db
    client = db.session.get(ApiClient, api_client_id)
    if client and client.created_by:
        return client.created_by
    # Fallback: return the client ID itself as actor (still traceable)
    return api_client_id


def get_api_scopes():
    """Return the scopes from the current API JWT context, or empty set."""
    return set(g.get("api_scopes", []))


def has_api_scope(scope):
    """Check if the current API context has a given scope."""
    return scope in get_api_scopes()


def is_safe_redirect_url(target):
    """Validate that a redirect target is a safe internal relative URL."""
    if not target:
        return False
    # Block absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, and javascript: schemes
    if target.startswith(("http://", "https://", "//", "javascript:")):
        return False
    # Must start with /
    if not target.startswith("/"):
        return False
    # Block backslash tricks
    if "\\" in target:
        return False
    return True
```

24	def get_kpis(report_scope, filters, user_permissions=None):
25	    fhash = _filters_hash(report_scope, filters)
26	    cache_key = f"kpi:{fhash}"
27	    cached = cache.get(cache_key)

29	        return cached
30	
31	    metrics = {}
32	    if report_scope in ("orders", "overview"):
33	        metrics.update(_order_kpis(filters))
34	    if report_scope in ("schedule", "overview"):

55	def _order_kpis(filters):
56	    q = Order.query
57	    if filters.get("region_id"):
58	        q = q.filter(Order.region_id == filters["region_id"])
59	    if filters.get("date_from"):
60	        q = q.filter(Order.created_at >= filters["date_from"])
61	    if filters.get("date_to"):
62	        q = q.filter(Order.created_at <= filters["date_to"])
63	    if filters.get("state"):
64	        q = q.filter(Order.state == filters["state"])
65	
66	    orders = q.all()
67	    total_count = len(orders)
68	    completed = [o for o in orders if o.completed_at]
69	    canceled = [o for o in orders if o.state == "canceled"]
70	    refunded = [o for o in orders if o.state == "refunded"]
71	
72	    turnaround_days = []
73	    for o in completed:
74	        if o.completed_at and o.created_at:
75	            td = (o.completed_at - o.created_at).total_seconds() / 86400
76	            turnaround_days.append(td)
77	
78	    on_time = sum(1 for o in completed
79	                  if o.scheduled_date and o.completed_at
80	                  and o.completed_at.date() <= o.scheduled_date)
81	
82	    exception_count = len(canceled) + len(refunded)
83	    total_revenue = sum(float(o.total_amount) for o in orders if o.state in ("paid", "completed"))
84	
85	    return {
86	        "order_count": total_count,
87	        "completed_count": len(completed),
88	        "avg_turnaround_days": round(sum(turnaround_days) / len(turnaround_days), 1) if turnaround_days else 0,
89	        "on_time_rate": round(on_time / len(completed) * 100, 1) if completed else 0,
90	        "exception_rate": round(exception_count / total_count * 100, 1) if total_count else 0,
91	        "total_revenue": round(total_revenue, 2),
92	    }

## Fix I: Scheduler duplication under multi-worker gunicorn

Read app/tasks/scheduler.py and run.py.

```python
"""Production/development entry point with scheduler.

Used by gunicorn: gunicorn "run:app"
Used locally:     python run.py

Scheduler design:
  The APScheduler background scheduler runs inside the gunicorn master process
  (or the single dev-server process). To prevent duplicate jobs under multi-worker
  deployment, gunicorn must NOT use --preload, and the scheduler is only started
  once via the module-level guard below. For production deployments that need
  isolated scheduling, set SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false and run a dedicated scheduler
  process:  python -m app.tasks.run_scheduler
"""

import os
from app import create_app
from app.tasks.scheduler import init_scheduler

app = create_app()

# Initialize FTS tables
with app.app_context():
    from app.services.search_service import init_fts
    init_fts(app)

# Start background scheduler only once.
# SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false disables it (for worker-only processes).
if os.environ.get("SCHEDULER_ENABLED", "true").lower() != "false":
    init_scheduler(app)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True, port=5000, use_reloader=False)
```

Also create app/tasks/run_scheduler.py as a standalone scheduler entrypoint:
```python
"""Standalone scheduler process.

Run this when web workers have SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false:
    python -m app.tasks.run_scheduler
"""

import time
from app import create_app
from app.tasks.scheduler import init_scheduler

app = create_app()

with app.app_context():
    from app.services.search_service import init_fts
    init_fts(app)

init_scheduler(app)
print("Scheduler running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.")

try:
    while True:
        time.sleep(60)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    from app.tasks.scheduler import scheduler
    scheduler.shutdown()
    print("Scheduler stopped.")
```

Now update docker-entrypoint.sh. Read it first, then update the gunicorn command to pass SCHEDULER_ENABLED only to the first worker. Actually, the simpler approach: since we use `--workers 2`, the scheduler starts in the master import. This is fine. But add the env var documentation. Replace the exec gunicorn line to add the comment and --preload flag:

Replace:
```bash
exec gunicorn \
    --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 \
    --workers 2 \
    --threads 4 \
    --timeout 120 \
    --access-logfile - \
    --error-logfile - \
    "run:app"
```

With:
```bash
# --preload ensures the app (and scheduler) is loaded once in the master process,
# preventing duplicate scheduler jobs across forked workers.
exec gunicorn \
    --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 \
    --workers 2 \
    --threads 4 \
    --timeout 120 \
    --preload \
    --access-logfile - \
    --error-logfile - \
    "run:app"
```

```markdown
# GreenCycle Operations & Content Portal

An offline-first Flask + HTMX application for municipal sustainability content management, operational scheduling, service catalog/order lifecycle, and analytics reporting.

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.12+
- pip

### Local Development

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Initialize the database
export FLASK_APP=wsgi.py
flask db upgrade

# Seed demo data (idempotent)
flask seed

# Run the development server (includes background scheduler)
python run.py
```

The app starts at **http://localhost:5000**.

### Docker

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

This builds the image, runs migrations, seeds data, and starts the app with gunicorn on port 5000.

## Demo Accounts

| Username | Password | Role |
|----------|----------|------|
| admin | admin123 | Full admin access |
| editor | editor123 | Content creation/editing |
| reviewer | reviewer123 | Content review/publish |
| dispatcher | dispatch123 | Resource/schedule management |
| analyst | analyst123 | Analytics/reporting (read-only) |

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` and set values. Key settings:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| SECRET_KEY | dev-secret | Flask session secret (change in production) |
| JWT_SECRET_KEY | dev-jwt-secret | API JWT signing key |
| FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY | (derived) | Fernet key for encrypted fields |
| SQLITE_PATH | instance/greencycle.db | Database file location |
| STORAGE_ROOT | storage | File upload/archive root |
| MAX_UPLOAD_MB | 20 | Max upload file size |
| API_DAILY_QUOTA | 1000 | API requests per key per day |
| SCHEDULER_ENABLED | true | Set false to disable background jobs |

See `.env.example` for the full list.

## Running Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

## Background Scheduler

The app runs four background jobs via APScheduler:

- **Scheduled Publish** (every 1 min): publishes content at scheduled times
- **Report Processor** (every 30 sec): processes queued CSV report jobs
- **Attachment Archive** (daily 2 AM): moves old uploads to archive
- **Attachment Purge** (daily 3 AM): deletes expired files if enabled

### Multi-worker deployment

When running with gunicorn, use `--preload` so the scheduler starts once in the master process. The Docker setup does this by default.

To run the scheduler as a separate process instead:

```bash
SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false gunicorn "run:app" --workers 4
python -m app.tasks.run_scheduler  # in a separate process
```

## Project Structure

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for detailed architecture.

See [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) for REST and GraphQL API documentation.

See [docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md) for implementation checklist.

## Offline-First

All assets (Bootstrap 5, HTMX, Quill editor) are bundled locally. No internet dependency for any feature.
```

Used by gunicorn: gunicorn "run:app"
Used locally:     python run.py

Scheduler design:
  The APScheduler background scheduler runs inside the gunicorn master process
  (or the single dev-server process). To prevent duplicate jobs under multi-worker
  deployment, gunicorn must NOT use --preload, and the scheduler is only started
  once via the module-level guard below. For production deployments that need
  isolated scheduling, set SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false and run a dedicated scheduler
  process:  python -m app.tasks.run_scheduler
"""

import os
from app import create_app
from app.tasks.scheduler import init_scheduler

app = create_app()

# Initialize FTS tables
with app.app_context():
    from app.services.search_service import init_fts
    init_fts(app)

# Start background scheduler only once.
# SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false disables it (for worker-only processes).
if os.environ.get("SCHEDULER_ENABLED", "true").lower() != "false":
    init_scheduler(app)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True, port=5000, use_reloader=False)
```

```markdown
# GreenCycle Operations & Content Portal

An offline-first Flask + HTMX application for municipal sustainability content management, operational scheduling, service catalog/order lifecycle, and analytics reporting.

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.12+
- pip

### Local Development

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Initialize the database
export FLASK_APP=wsgi.py
flask db upgrade

# Seed demo data (idempotent)
flask seed

# Run the development server (includes background scheduler)
python run.py
```

The app starts at **http://localhost:5000**.

### Docker

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

This builds the image, runs migrations, seeds data, and starts the app with gunicorn on port 5000.

## Demo Accounts

| Username | Password | Role |
|----------|----------|------|
| admin | admin123 | Full admin access |
| editor | editor123 | Content creation/editing |
| reviewer | reviewer123 | Content review/publish |
| dispatcher | dispatch123 | Resource/schedule management |
| analyst | analyst123 | Analytics/reporting (read-only) |

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` and set values. Key settings:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| SECRET_KEY | dev-secret | Flask session secret (change in production) |
| JWT_SECRET_KEY | dev-jwt-secret | API JWT signing key |
| FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY | (derived) | Fernet key for encrypted fields |
| SQLITE_PATH | instance/greencycle.db | Database file location |
| STORAGE_ROOT | storage | File upload/archive root |
| MAX_UPLOAD_MB | 20 | Max upload file size |
| API_DAILY_QUOTA | 1000 | API requests per key per day |
| SCHEDULER_ENABLED | true | Set false to disable background jobs |

See `.env.example` for the full list.

## Running Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

## Background Scheduler

The app runs four background jobs via APScheduler:

- **Scheduled Publish** (every 1 min): publishes content at scheduled times
- **Report Processor** (every 30 sec): processes queued CSV report jobs
- **Attachment Archive** (daily 2 AM): moves old uploads to archive
- **Attachment Purge** (daily 3 AM): deletes expired files if enabled

### Multi-worker deployment

When running with gunicorn, use `--preload` so the scheduler starts once in the master process. The Docker setup does this by default.

To run the scheduler as a separate process instead:

```bash
SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false gunicorn "run:app" --workers 4
python -m app.tasks.run_scheduler  # in a separate process
```

## Project Structure

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for detailed architecture.

See [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) for REST and GraphQL API documentation.

See [docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md) for implementation checklist.

## Offline-First

All assets (Bootstrap 5, HTMX, Quill editor) are bundled locally. No internet dependency for any feature.

Covers: JWT file download, outbox consumer isolation, cost KPIs, report filters,
